title: 11 foreign keys have no index in PostgreSQL, so one endpoint is 450 times slower
summary: MySQL creates an index for each foreign key, but PostgreSQL does not. Build the 11 missing indexes after the bulk copy and before the CDC catch-up.

blocks.title: The problem
blocks.html: MySQL (InnoDB) creates an index for each foreign key without a request. PostgreSQL does not. The schema conversion copied the foreign keys, but not these hidden indexes.

blocks.title: What we found
blocks.html:
• [TESTED] The converted schema has 23 foreign keys. 11 of them have no index. [src: report.md]
  • [TESTED] In staging, GET /orders/{id}/items took 4,100 ms at p95. On MySQL it takes 9 ms. With the index, it took 7 ms. [src: report.md]
  • [TESTED] In staging, the 11 indexes took 11 minutes to build. [src: report.md]
  • [INFERRED] At full size, the build takes about 1 h 50 min. [src: report.md]

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.html: The order page and the support dashboard use this endpoint. Staging holds only 10% of the rows. At full size, the endpoint without the index is slower than in staging. [INFERRED]

blocks.title: Proposed action
blocks.html: Add the 11 indexes to the migration script. Build them after the bulk copy and before the CDC catch-up. Effort: 1 day.

options.label: Build the indexes after the copy, before the catch-up
options.detail_html: Effort: 1 day. The copy keeps its speed (about 5 h 30 min). The build adds about 1 h 50 min. With CDC (D1 option b), the shop stays open during both steps.

options.label: Create the indexes before the copy
options.detail_html: Effort: half a day. The script is simpler. The copy becomes about 40% slower (+2 h 10 min). If you select D1 option a, this time adds to the downtime.

recommendation_html: Option a. The total time is shorter, and the downtime stays short with each D1 option.
